title: Ducks Unlimited collaboration helps protect Louisiana wetlands
summary: What wetland conservation means for wildlife, local communities and future generations.
body_markdown:
What wetland conservation means for wildlife, local communities and future generations


For more than a decade, Phillips 66 has collaborated with Ducks Unlimited to conserve and restore wetlands across the United States.


**Why it matters**


Phillips 66 is committed to advancing[sustainability](https://www.phillips66.com/sustainability/) and strengthening the environmental resilience of our[communities](https://www.phillips66.com/social-impact/) through investments in flood mitigation, nature preservation, wildlife support, overall ecosystem enhancement and costal conservation.


Since 2013, conservation projects have impacted over 44,000 acres of wetlands, including shoreline protection, marsh terracing and water management improvements that help strengthen habitats along the Gulf Coast.


---


Follow Ducks Unlimited and Phillips 66 representatives across the wetlands of southern Louisiana to learn about the importance of protecting these habitats and how these efforts benefit wildlife, coastal ecosystems and local communities for generations to come.


**Featuring:** Matt Bunn, managing director of development, Ducks Unlimited; Scot Tyler, vice president, Phillips 66 Lake Charles Refinery; Bob Dew, manager of conservation programs, Ducks Unlimited; and Mickey McMillin, Phillips 66 community advisory panel member and longtime Ducks Unlimited volunteer.


*Visit the*[Phillips 66 community](https://www.phillips66.com/safety/social-impact/) *page to learn more about the company’s commitment to helping build stronger, safer and more resilient communities.*
